Mario Party 4 PowerPC Edition -- the port layer
================================================

The port layer (everything under port/ in the source tree: the host loop,
the module loader, the disc, the memory card, the controller, the CPU
audio mixer, the GX-to-OpenGL renderer and the render thread) was written
for one person's own Power Mac G4.  It is not for redistribution, and it
carries no game data: the disc image is the player's own.

Source: https://github.com/southcitycapture/mp4ppcosx10 (branch ppc-port)

The game's own code is compiled as is from the mariopartyrd/marioparty4
decompilation (https://github.com/mariopartyrd/marioparty4), whose
repository carries no licence file; nothing of the decompilation's source
is edited in this port, and where the game's behaviour has to change for
the port it is changed through exact-text substitutions applied at build
time (port/patches.txt).  Mario Party 4 is the property of Nintendo and
Hudson Soft.

The THP movie decoder (port/src/thp) is the port's own; its inverse DCT,
Huffman lookahead tables and sign-extension trick follow stb_image by Sean
Barrett, under the MIT licence (see "stb_image (MIT).txt").

The MusyX audio library is Axiomatic Data Laboratories' reimplementation,
under the MIT licence (see "MusyX (MIT).txt").  SDL2 is under the zlib
licence (see "SDL2 (zlib).txt"); the copy in the application is built
from the panther-sdl2 tree for Mac OS X 10.4 on PowerPC.

No Dolphin emulator code is used.  Dolphin was the reference the port's
pictures were compared against.
